title: Mapping Data to Components Practice
summary: Practice challenge: build an 'emojipedia' card dictionary by extracting a repeated block of HTML into an Entry component, replacing the hard-coded text with props, and rendering one Entry per object in emojipedia.js with map(). The solution half shows how to break the problem into numbered steps and work through them.

concepts.heading: Starting project
points: Fork the CodeSandbox from the course resources (or use the local Vite version). public/ already has index.html with the Montserrat Google Font link, styles.css and the root div; index.js renders <App/>. Nothing in public needs changing.

App.jsx contains a long block of static HTML: an h1 with a span reading 'emojipedia', then a <dl className="dictionary"> holding three near-identical <div className="term"> blocks (Tense Biceps, Person With Folded Hands, Rolling On The Floor Laughing).
emojipedia.js holds a const array of three objects, each with id, emoji, name and meaning. It is not exported yet.
The supplied styles.css produces the finished card look, but the styling is optional; the point is the mapping.

concepts.heading: Description list elements: dl, dt, dd
points: <dl> is a description list: a container for groups of terms and their descriptions, such as a glossary or dictionary.
<dt> is the term being described; <dd> is the description or detail for it. A dt/dd pair works rather like a key-value pair.
Grouping a dt and its dd in a <div> is allowed inside a dl, which is what the starter does with div.term so each pair can be styled as a card.
The emoji is in <span className="emoji" role="img" aria-label="..."> so screen readers announce a label instead of the raw character.

concepts.heading: Planning: split a big challenge into small steps
points: The challenge comes without step comments, so write your own: break the end result into small tasks you can tick off.
Step 1: extract the repeated part (each div.term) into its own Entry component.
Step 2: find what differs between the repeats (emoji, name, meaning) and replace each with a prop.
Step 3a: export the emojipedia array and import it into App.
Step 3b: map over the array and render an Entry per object, with a key.

concepts.heading: Step 1: extracting Entry
points: Create Entry.jsx with the usual component boilerplate (import React, function Entry, export default Entry) and import Entry into App.jsx.
Cut one whole <div className="term"> out of App and return it from Entry; delete the other two copies but keep the surrounding <dl className="dictionary"> in App.
Temporarily place <Entry /> three times inside the dl. The page shows three identical cards, which proves the extraction worked.

concepts.heading: Step 2: props for the parts that change
points: Choose clear prop names. The solution uses emoji, name and description.
In Entry, accept props and swap the hard-coded values for {props.emoji}, {props.name} and {props.description}, each in curly braces.
Test by passing hard-coded strings (copied from emojipedia.js) to the first <Entry/> only. That card fills in while the other two render empty, because no props reach them.
Writing out props for every Entry by hand would work but is exactly the repetition map() removes.

concepts.heading: Step 3: import the data and map it
points: A value can only be imported if its file exports it: add export default emojipedia; at the bottom of emojipedia.js.
In App.jsx (inside the components folder in the sandbox) write import emojipedia from "../emojipedia"; the ../ steps up from components into src.
console.log(emojipedia) is a quick check that the array of three objects (id, emoji, name, meaning) arrived.
Delete the placeholder Entry elements and write {emojipedia.map(createEntry)} inside the dl, wrapped in curly braces so it runs as JavaScript.
createEntry(emojiTerm) receives one object per call and returns <Entry key={emojiTerm.id} emoji={emojiTerm.emoji} name={emojiTerm.name} description={emojiTerm.meaning} />.
The key prop is required whenever components are produced by looping over an array; id is unique, so it is used.
Pasting one sample object as a comment next to createEntry is a handy reference while matching data fields to prop names.
Result: as many cards as objects in the array. Adding a new object (e.g. another emoji and its meaning) to emojipedia.js makes a new card appear with no extra JSX.
(Extra) map() is used here instead of forEach because map returns the new array of <Entry/> elements, which JSX can render directly; forEach returns undefined, so nothing would appear.

task.name: Emojipedia: map data to Entry components
task.starting_point: Forked sandbox with App.jsx holding three hard-coded div.term cards inside a dl, emojipedia.js with an unexported array of {id, emoji, name, meaning}, and finished styles.css/index.html.
task.goal: Render the dictionary entirely from emojipedia.js so that adding an object to the array adds a card automatically.
steps: Write your own step list before coding (extract, add props, import, map).
Create Entry.jsx, move one div.term into it and return it; import Entry into App.
Remove the other hard-coded cards, keeping the dl wrapper in App.
Replace the emoji, name and meaning text in Entry with {props.emoji}, {props.name} and {props.description}.
Add export default emojipedia; to emojipedia.js and import it in App with the correct relative path.
Write createEntry(emojiTerm) returning an Entry with key, emoji, name and description (= emojiTerm.meaning).
Add a fourth emoji object to the array to confirm a new card appears with no JSX changes.
task.expected_result: Styled 'emojipedia' heading followed by one white card per array item (large emoji, teal name, description), with no key warning in the console.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 36 - React.js/36.22 Mapping Data to Components Practice/mapping-components-practice/src/App.jsx

pitfalls: Forgetting to export emojipedia before importing it (the import is undefined).
Wrong relative path: App.jsx sits in components, so the data file is ../emojipedia.
Leaving out the curly braces around emojipedia.map(...) in JSX.
Using a data field name as a prop name by mistake: the prop is description but the object field is meaning.
Moving the dl into Entry, which creates a separate description list per card instead of one list of terms.
Leaving aria-label hard-coded as 'Tense Biceps' for every card. (Extra) Use aria-label={props.name} so each emoji has the right accessible label.

(Extra) Reference repo divergence: the student's App.jsx maps the array twice (once with an arrow function block and once with a concise arrow), so every card appears twice; delete one. It also uses key={index} instead of the id, passes the prop as meaning, and puts a <dl> inside each Entry. The lecture's version uses a named createEntry function, key={emojiTerm.id}, the description prop and a single dl in App.

gaps_and_ideas: New lesson 'Emojipedia: mapping practice' (s36). Blurb: extract a repeated card into a component, drive it with props, and render it from an array with map().
Task 1: extract the repeated div.term into an Entry component and render it three times.
Task 2: add emoji, name and description props and fill one Entry with hard-coded values.
Task 3: export the emojipedia array and import it into App.
Task 4: render {emojipedia.map(createEntry)} with key={emojiTerm.id} and description={emojiTerm.meaning}.
Task 5 (stretch): add your own emoji object and confirm the card appears; set aria-label from props.
Starter code: App.jsx with the three hard-coded dl/dt/dd cards, emojipedia.js with an unexported array, and the supplied styles.css.

Interactive demo: a small form (emoji, name, meaning) that pushes into the array and shows the new card instantly, with a side panel listing the array beside the rendered cards so learners see one object per card.
Explore panel: a short dl/dt/dd explainer with an MDN link, since these elements have not appeared earlier in the course.
